recentItems.title: How to Make a Screenprint | Step-by-Step Tutorial
recentItems.description:
Learn how to screenprint with artist Rob Swainston in this hands-on tutorial. He will walk you through the entire silkscreen process, from hand-drawn and photo-based transparencies to exposing screens, mixing ink to make custom colors, and pulling multiple layers by hand.

You'll learn:
The history of silkscreen — from simple paper stencils (pochoir) to photo emulsion techniques
How to build transparencies by hand-drawing on a light table (no fancy equipment needed — just a clip light, plexiglass, or a trash can!)
Turning photographs into silkscreen-ready images using grayscale, bitmap conversion, and halftone dot patterns
Choosing the right mesh count for your screen based on detail and image type
Coating a screen with photo emulsion using a scoop coater
Exposing, rinsing, and reclaiming screens for reuse
Mixing acrylic inks to build custom colors
Registration techniques for lining up multiple color layers
Squeegee technique: flooding the screen, pulling ink, and printing multiple passes
How layering transparent colors creates richer, more complex imagery than opaque printing


Whether you're combining hand drawing with photography, working in a home studio, or a professional print shop, this tutorial covers the full screenprinting workflow from a single sketch to a finished multi-layer print.

Artists and references mentioned: Corita Kent, Emory Douglas, Robert Rauschenberg, Romare Bearden, and Andy Warhol.

00:00 Introduction to silkscreen & its history
01:48  Building hand-drawn transparencies
03:07 Turning photographs into silkscreen images (grayscale & bitmap)
06:35 Layering transparencies 
07:43 Choosing mesh count for your screen
08:35 Coating a screen with photo emulsion
11:00 Exposing and rinsing the screen
12:50 Mixing transparent inks
17:26 Printing: flooding, squeegee technique, and pulling prints
25:00 Layering colors & building the final image

If you're interested in learning silkscreen printing, photo emulsion techniques, or how to combine drawing and photography in printmaking, this tutorial is for you.

recentItems.title: What is the readymade?
recentItems.description:
Brush up on your art terms! 

Readymade is a term coined by Marcel Duchamp in 1916 to describe prefabricated, often mass-produced objects isolated from their intended use and elevated to the status of art by the artist choosing and designating them as such.

recentItems.title: How to Make Hand-Drawn Animation | Straight-Ahead and Keyframing
recentItems.description:
Learn how to make hand-drawn animation from start to finish. In this tutorial, animator Kohana Wilson (they/them) walks through the tools, techniques, and principles behind classic paper animation, from your very first drawn frame to a finished animated sequence in After Effects. Whether you're animating an abstract dot, a dragonfly, or a cartwheeling character, this video breaks down the full traditional animation workflow — from rough sketches to a polished, moving sequence.

You'll learn:
- The science behind animation — persistence of vision, explained with a zoetrope, praxinoscope, and flip book
- Essential tools: light boxes, peg bars, and paper choices for hand-drawn animation
- Straight-ahead animation — drawing frame by frame in sequence
- Keyframe animation and in-betweening — planning key poses first, then filling in the motion
- Core animation principles: squash and stretch, easing in and out, follow-through, overlapping action, and smear frames
- How to clean up rough animation and scan your frames for digital editing
- Bringing your sequence to life in Adobe After Effects

Artwork references included: Lotte Reiniger, John Canemaker, Winsor McCay, David Ehrlich, Eadweard J. Muybridge, Mary Beams, Maria Lassnig, and William Kentridge.

00:00 Introduction to animation and optical toys
02:42 Tools you need: light box, paper, peg bars
04:16 Straight-ahead animation demo
06:31 Animation principles: squash and stretch, follow-through
13:32 Keyframe animation & in-betweening
20:11 Cleaning up rough animation
21:32 Scanning frames and editing in After Effects

If you're interested in learning traditional 2D animation, hand-drawn character animation, or the fundamentals every animator should know, this tutorial is for you.
